<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/ui/action-confirm-beside-params.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aad1603cc2180b3eefa8cee41f5b895b8ee45909` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4fdac8501027eb012d47a4cc0af01eb3f2bc5e66` — the merge of head `9d69f747cd545a5e11690329ea16436a77d8a49a` into base `aad1603cc2180b3eefa8cee41f5b895b8ee45909`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4fdac8501027eb012d47a4cc0af01eb3f2bc5e66 && git checkout 4fdac8501027eb012d47a4cc0af01eb3f2bc5e66
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin aad1603cc2180b3eefa8cee41f5b895b8ee45909 9d69f747cd545a5e11690329ea16436a77d8a49a && git checkout -B drift-repro aad1603cc2180b3eefa8cee41f5b895b8ee45909 && git merge --no-ff 9d69f747cd545a5e11690329ea16436a77d8a49a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aad1603cc2180b3eefa8cee41f5b895b8ee45909
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs aad1603cc2180b3eefa8cee41f5b895b8ee45909` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The face: `--paths` returns `hits` = `component.zod.ts` (published schema source); the PR body and changeset both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, so the tier is CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER on either face.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **What is newly refused, exactly.** Three rows gain one `.refine` at the end of their chain, whose predicate is the negation of `declaresConfirmBesideParams(row)` and whose issue is `CONFIRM_BESIDE_PARAMS_REFUSAL`: `ActionIconPropsSchema` (L4189), the `action:group` member (L4432) and the `action:menu` member (L4465). The predicate is the one `action:button` reads: `confirmText` neither null nor undefined, and `params` an array of positive length. So the only authored values newly refused are `confirmText` (bare string or the `{ dialect: 'template', source }` envelope — both `!= null`) beside an array `params` of length at least one, on an `action:icon`'s `properties` and on each member of an `action:group` / `action:menu` `properties.actions`. Right, and it is the ruling's letter A exactly.
2. **What is still accepted, exactly.** No `params` (undefined, not an array); `params: []` (length 0); an object `params` (not an array) — on the icon the static values, on a `type: 'api'` member the request payload; and every `confirmText` form on those three shapes. The guard test's two acceptance groups pin all four of these per door with a full `safeParse` success. A blank `confirmText` (`''`) beside an array is refused, as on the other three doors; a locale-map `confirmText` is refused by the template slot before the predicate runs. Right.
3. **One predicate, one message.** Both symbols are imported once (L71) and used four times; `component.zod.ts` carries no second literal of the message (0 hits for `TWO dialogs` outside the import's source). The new tests pin each door's message `toBe` `action:button`'s own issue, which the earlier group pins `toBe` `ActionSchema`'s and `InlineActionSchema`'s. Five doors, one wording. Right.
4. **The member issue path.** The refusal's own `path` is `['confirmText']`; it is attached to the member schema, and `ActionGroupPropsSchema.actions` / `ActionMenuPropsSchema.actions` are `z.array(actionGroupMember())` / `z.array(actionMenuMember())`, so zod prefixes the element index: `['actions', i, 'confirmText']` on both containers. The test pins index 1 on both (the offending member is the second). `validateComponentProps` joins it under the node's `properties`, so the finding lands at `….properties.actions.N.confirmText` (and `….properties.confirmText` on the icon), which is what the dev's door probe printed. Right.
5. **Interplay with `actionContainerMemberParamsFitType`.** That refine returns early on `params === undefined || Array.isArray(params) || type === 'api'`, and refuses at `['params']` otherwise. The two refines are disjoint on the `params` axis: an array `params` is fit-type-silent and pair-judged; a non-array `params` on a non-`api` member is fit-type-refused and pair-silent (`Array.isArray` is false); an object `params` on an `api` member passes both. No row gets two verdicts for one fact, and no previously-accepted shape outside the ruling is newly refused. Right.
6. **The remedy key exists on every door.** `description` is declared on the icon row (L4153: "the tooltip text when there is no `label`, and forwarded to the runner for the parameter dialog") and on the member shape (L4313: "the parameter dialog shows it under its title"); `action-icon.tsx`, `action-group.tsx` and `action-menu.tsx` forward it as `description` to the runner, whose param dialog draws it. The message's prescription is actionable on all three rows. Right.
7. **The measurement grounding the ruling holds in the cited code.** `action-icon.tsx` forwards an array `params` as `actionParams` and `confirmText` as itself; `action-group.tsx` L350-352/L380 and `action-menu.tsx` L273-275/L312 do the same per member; `ActionRunner.execute` L1675-1684 awaits the confirm, then L1690-1693 reads `actionParams` and opens the param dialog when its length is positive. Two dialogs, in that order, for exactly the shape refused. Right.
8. **Public surface and types.** Each of the three schemas was already a refined object (four `superRefine`s), so one more `.refine` changes no `z.input` / `z.output` type, no `ComponentPropsMap` row and no export; `api-surface/` and `authorable-surface/` are untouched in the diff, and `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` already lists `ui/ActionIconProps`, `ui/ActionGroupProps` and `ui/ActionMenuProps`. No authorable key moves. Right.
9. **Describe and generated docs.** The icon's and the member shape's `confirmText` describe append `action:button`'s sentence, the member variant naming the `type: 'api'` payload (true per 5); `ACTION_ROW_COPY_DESCRIBE.confirmText` stays shared and unchanged. The three `component.mdx` rows reflect those describes verbatim and nothing else moves in that file. No tracker id in any runtime string (the refusal message and the three describes carry none; `#30017` appears in comments only). Right.
10. **Census carrier repaired honestly.** The pin test's "a member with every forwarded scalar" keeps `confirmText` and loses its `params`; a new case "a member collecting params" carries the array with `description`. Both still parse byte-identical. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the `**BREAKING**` banner, the `fix(spec)!:` summary, exactly one `adr-0087` marker, the same two declaration lines on the PR body. AGENTS.md step 3: a kind takes at least `minor` on the moved package; `narrowed` is the right kind ("a value refused … is `narrowed`"); `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and the banner is present. The `Check Changeset` run on the head (both checkers) concluded `success`. Level, kind and arm: correct.
- **The ADR-0087 disposition is not honest for this refusal — must-fix.** The marker reads `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` and its `why` argues that no key is added, removed or renamed and that "there is no rewrite that keeps what the author meant without reading it, so the author decides, and the refusal names the remedy". That is an argument for no D2 *conversion*. ADR-0087 D3 says that exact shape is what a *semantic entry* is for: "A migration that cannot be expressed declaratively gets a structured TODO entry (surface, reason, acceptance criteria) rather than silence, so the agent knows exactly what judgment is being delegated to it", and `SemanticMigration`'s docblock: "One retirement family's D3 entry — owed even when a lossless D2 conversion carries the data repair … (ADR-0087 D3: 'never silence')". The ledger's own practice on these very rows confirms it: `18.ui-page-action-row-on-success-beside-executor-refused.ts` registers "`onSuccess` beside an executor other than `api` / `script` on an `action:button` / `action:icon` and each `action:group` / `action:menu` member", explicitly "⛔ NOT mechanically convertible … the author's call", with "Measured producers: none"; and `18.ui-action-group-menu-member-params-array-only.ts` registers a member `params` refusal "D3 only … there is no D2 conversion … and the census found no writer to respell". A pair refusal on the same rows, with a hand remedy and a zero census, is the same class, and this changeset's body *carries* that remedy ("**The remedy.** Move the confirm sentence to the action's `description` … and drop `confirmText`") — the category's own definition in the gate (L147-152: a body "that ships instructions for rewriting a consumer's code cannot also claim no consumer has to rewrite anything") says the two cannot coexist. The gate let it through only because `findMigrationPrescription` reads arrow-form and framed-table rewrites, not a "The remedy." paragraph; ADR-0087's #8299 addendum (the disposition vocabulary) names an exemption "held by a DETECTOR MISS, not by a positive finding" as the anti-pattern this vocabulary exists to close. PR #29869 is the precedent the changeset cites, and it did ship this way (`CHANGELOG.md` L2321, in the released 18.x line, as #29383 did at L2148) — that makes the omission two doors wide, not honest. What the consumer loses: an upgrader carrying the pair on an icon or a member gets no `os migrate meta` TODO for step 18; the first word is the save-door refusal. **Fix:** one D3-only entry `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-page-action-row-confirm-text-beside-params-refused.ts` in the shape of the `on-success-beside-executor-refused` entry — surface: `properties.confirmText` beside a non-empty array `properties.params` on an `action:button` or `action:icon`, and `confirmText` beside a non-empty array `params` on each `action:group` / `action:menu` member; replacement: the question on `description`, `confirmText` dropped (the icon tooltip note from the changeset belongs in `reason`); reason: the runner order and the save-door read; acceptance: `os validate` reports no `component-props-invalid` at those paths. Naming all four rows closes #29869's gap in the same family entry. Then the marker becomes `registered ui-page-action-row-confirm-text-beside-params-refused` (the registration gate verifies the id resolves at HEAD and is new in the diff; `gen:migration-registry` reads the directory, and runs under build, test and typecheck). The changeset text otherwise stands.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev "stopped on": the `action-confirm-beside-params.ts` docblock still says "read by the three doors", "asserts the three messages equal", "on all three doors".** Confirmed stale at the head (L5-6, L8-9, L16-17 of that module): five doors now read it. It is a comment; the claim's file surface admitted the module only for a message variant, which was not needed, so the dev was right to stop. Should-fix, on this PR's fix round (the seat owns the claim and can widen the surface by one comment block): count five doors and name the two new rows. No behaviour rides on it.
2. **Dev "stopped on": the `description` remedy changes a label-less icon's tooltip.** Confirmed in the cited renderer: `action-icon.tsx` wraps the button in a tooltip reading `schema.label || schema.description`, and `aria-label` is `schema.label || schema.name`, so on an icon with no `label` the moved question becomes the hover text (the accessible name does not move). The icon row's own `description` describe already declares that dual role (L4153), the renderer's `description` input says the same, and the changeset's remedy line states the side effect. The author's escape is to give the icon a `label`. A renderer fact outside the ruling, not a spec defect; answered, no change asked. Should-fix (optional, wording only): the icon's `confirmText` describe could end "on a label-less icon `description` is also the tooltip, so give it a `label`" — the changeset already says it, so this is not required.
3. **`check:dev-prereqs` exit 1 (35 `ui/` packages without `dist`).** A local-only family that judges whether that checkout can boot a dev server; it is not derived for this diff and no check-run carries it. Answered: machine state.
4. **`open_questions`: none.** Answered.
5. **`out_of_scope_findings`: the docblock in 1.** Answered there.
6. **Skills-docs claim.** `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` L22 ("A registered action is refused it beside a non-empty `params` (put the question on `description`)") stays a true sentence and names this refusal's remedy; it is a Tier H path and outside this PR. Answered.
7. **Check-runs on `0446795a12` at the second read.** Concluded `success`: Auto Label, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI/release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped (query-options erasure; slot lookup & corpus; tooling self-tests), Live E2E UI, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates (carries `check:docs` and `check:authorable-surface`), filter. `skipped`: 18.x upgrade harness, Dogfood shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Packed-tarball smoke, Schedule gate, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts. Still `in_progress`, no conclusion: Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates (carries `check:api-surface`), Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · workspace. Nothing failed. Reported as seen, not waited for; the PR body's local readings (25669 spec tests, 102 derived families at exit 0, the three ablation legs, the door probe) are the dev's account and are not adopted here.
8. **Governed surfaces.** None of the five paths is under `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md` or `.github/workflows/**`; the Governed Surface Queue Guard concluded `success`. The fix in ② adds a file under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`, which is not a governed surface either.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` — holds; the must-fix is on the changeset it ships with, not on the schema.** Judged against ruling 6624208841 letter A and its first consumers (the lint `validateComponentProps` door at the CLI commands and the runtime `page` save; the `action:icon`, `action:group` and `action:menu` renderers through `ActionRunner`).
- *Does it make the spec's own refusal real at the consumer?* Yes. The door dispatches each node's `properties` to `ComponentPropsMap[type].safeParse` and reports each issue at `properties` + the issue path under `component-props-invalid`, so the icon's lands at `properties.confirmText` and a member's at `properties.actions.N.confirmText`, with the message naming the `description` remedy that every one of the three rows declares and forwards. A stored page keeps loading (the load path parses no component `properties`), and its next save is refused — the same read as the four sibling step-18 entries on these rows state.
- *Does it take a declared capability away beyond the ruling?* No. The predicate's `Array.isArray` + positive-length read is the complete reading of "non-empty array"; the four controls per door pin the kept shapes (① 2), and the fit-type refine stays the sole judge of a non-array `params` on a non-`api` member (① 5).
- *Attempts to break it.* (a) The member alias table (`ACTION_CONTAINER_MEMBER_ALIASES`) folds `actionType` → `type` and the target spellings; it never renames `params` or `confirmText`, so the predicate sees the authored pair. (b) Each `superRefine` before the `.refine` adds issues without `fatal`, so the pair refusal is reported beside any other row verdict rather than hidden behind it; the tests read the issue by path, not index, and the pair-only fixtures assert exactly one issue. (c) `action:bar` members are `ActionSchema` rows, which already refuse the pair, so no composition that reaches these renderers through the bar is newly refused there. (d) A member with `confirmText` and an object `params` on a non-`api` type draws the fit-type verdict alone; once the author turns `params` into an array the pair verdict appears — two rounds, but each verdict is true when given and the second is the ruling's; not a defect. (e) The `lazySchema` wrappers and the `*MemberOnce` caches are unchanged, so the refine is built once per member schema and the `ActionGroupProps` / `ActionMenuProps` `actions` arrays share it.
- *Must-fix:* none in this file.
- *Should-fix:* none in this file; the docblock count in ③ 1 lives in the sibling module.
